item.title: Periodic Table
item.description: Definition The periodic table organizes Elements into 18 vertical Groups and 7 horizontal Periods.

item.title: 09 Periodic Trends
item.description: Overview The experimental basis of the Periodic Table of the Elements is the Periodic Law: Certain Properties reoccur periodically when the elements are arranged by increasing Atomic Number.

item.title: Colloids
item.description: Definition A colloid is a Mixture in which one Substance, consisting of microscopically dispersed Insoluble particles, is suspended throughout another substance.

item.title: Colligative Property
item.description: Definition Colligative properties are Physical Properties of Solutions that depend solely on the ratio of the number of Solute particles to Solvent particles, not the nature or identity of the solute.

item.title: Osmotic Pressure
item.description: Definition Osmotic pressure \Pi, is the Minimum Pressure required to stop the flow of pure Solvent across a semipermeable Membrane into a Solution.

item.title: Reverse Osmosis
item.description: Definition Reverse osmosis is a highly effective Water purification process that used Pressure to force water through a semipermeable Membrane, separating it from contaminants, like Salts, bacteria and chemicals.

item.title: 14 Solutions
item.description: Overview In a Solution, the Solvent, usually the component present in greatest amounts, determines the State of Matter in which the solution exists.

item.title: Membrane
item.description: Definition A membrane is a selective barrier, it allows some things to pass through but stops others (Molecules, Ions or other small particles).

item.title: Osmosis
item.description: Definition Osmosis is the Spontaneous movement of Solvent Molecules (usually Water) through a semipermeable Membrane from a region of low Solute Concentration to high solute concentration.
